sampling_model.design: Observational sampling from a fixed population law; population partial identification is primary and frontier inference is secondary.
sampling_model.units: Independent draws \((X_i,A_i,Y_i)\sim P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) with finite \(\mathcal X\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment may depend on \((X,U)\); every candidate full-data law restores conditional ignorability given the same binary \(U\) for both potential outcomes.
sampling_model.overlap: Every observed stratum satisfies \(0<p_x<1\) and \(0<r_{a,x}<1\).  At finite budgets, every sharp endpoint is attained with \(0<w_{a,x}<1\): nontrivial endpoints use an interior point of the canonical arc, and point-identified exceptions use \(w_{0,x}=w_{1,x}=1/2\).  Vanishing latent treatment positivity appears only along the joint all-budget path used for Manski recovery.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The finite-cell summaries \((\lambda_x,p_x,r_{0,x},r_{1,x})\) are estimated by empirical frequencies.  At a unique nondegenerate active branch with nonzero budget gradient, the regular inference theorem gives the explicit root-\(n\) normal displacement and standard-error constant; uniform inference is open only at optimizer ties, legal-root collisions, stationary continua, and higher-order algebraic contact.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: For fixed sensitivity parameters, the binary mixtures have unique maximum-likelihood solutions and yield a recalculated average treatment effect.
Quantile balancing gives the sharp ATE interval under the marginal sensitivity model.

For binary or low-level categorical exposure and binary outcome, an exposure-standardization sensitivity function is variation-independent of the observed-data distribution and supports three consistent estimators of marginal causal effects.
General bias formulas specialize to outcome contrasts multiplied by changes in the distribution of a binary confounder.
A sharp joint relative-risk bounding factor applies to an unrestricted unmeasured confounder.
A breakdown frontier is the boundary between assumptions that do and do not support a chosen conclusion.
With no restriction on treatment selection, binary potential-outcome means obey worst-case treatment-response bounds.

tldr: For binary treatment, outcome, and one shared latent binary confounder within finitely many observed strata, the causal ATE image is exactly the same interval \([L,R]\) over the strictly positive class and its finite-simplex closure.  Both arms are optimized at one common posterior pair.  A strict tilt-gap derivative argument reduces every non-point-identified stratum endpoint to the canonical arc \(w_0=W_{\Gamma_A}(t),w_1=t\) with \(0<t<1\); point-identified exceptions are attained by \(w_0=w_1=1/2\), so closure is not needed for endpoint attainment.  The fixed-input certificate and parametric tipping atlas operate one-dimensionally while retaining denominator checks, legal-root collisions, and stationary continua.  The complete rational transcript \((\mathrm{C1})\)--\((\mathrm{C10})\) certifies a stable strict gap relative to the internal separate-pair relaxation.  Regular zero-frontier points have the proved root-\(n\) normal-displacement law, while uniformly honest inference at ties, collisions, continua, and higher-order contact remains the singular-only open question.

project_justification.gap: The fixed-tuple binary-confounder calculation of Rosenbaum and Rubin does not optimize this maintained bounded common-posterior region or prove its positive-class endpoint attainment.  Propensity-only, arbitrary-confounder, and exposure-standardization models use different primitives.  Absent an observable-law-dependent translation, the paper asserts no nesting or numerical-dominance relation between those published models and the maintained class.
project_justification.niche: The restriction is scientifically interpretable and algebraically low dimensional: strict coordinate monotonicity reduces shared-posterior optimization to one exposure-odds arc, places every nontrivial endpoint at an interior posterior pair, and preserves the compatibility information removed by the armwise relaxation.
project_justification.fill: The paper supplies the exact equality \(\tau(\mathcal M^{\circ})=\tau(\mathcal M)=[L,R]\), strictly positive endpoint-attaining laws, a canonical one-arc reduction, a degeneracy-complete fixed-input certificate, a parametric algebraic tipping atlas, the complete \((\mathrm{C1})\)--\((\mathrm{C10})\) strict-gap witness, point-identification and Manski-limit reductions, and pointwise regular-frontier inference; only singular uniform frontier inference remains open.

related_work: Rosenbaum and Rubin \cite{RosenbaumRubin1983Sensitivity} are retained only as the fixed-tuple binary-confounder comparator; the verified source does not establish equality with, or an inclusion direction for, this paper's arm-specific two-sided bounded class, arbitrary conditional potential-outcome coupling, or finite-simplex closure.  VanderWeele and Arah \cite{VanderWeeleArah2011Bias} motivate the binary-confounder bias decomposition.  Ding and VanderWeele \cite{DingVanderWeele2016WithoutAssumptions} give a sharp arbitrary-\(U\) relative-risk factor, while Tan \cite{Tan2006MarginalSensitivity}, Yadlowsky et al. \cite{YadlowskyEtAl2022Bounds}, and Dorn and Guo \cite{DornGuo2023QuantileBalancing} study propensity-based marginal sensitivity models.  Ciocănea-Teodorescu, Gabriel, and Sjölander \cite{CiocaneaGabrielSjolander2022Marginal} use exposure-standardization sensitivity parameters, and Nabi et al. \cite{NabiEtAl2024SemiparametricSensitivity} provide an adjacent tilt-model framework.  Absent a proved observable-law-dependent translation, no nesting or numerical-dominance relation is asserted between any of those published models and the maintained common-binary-\(U\) class.  The separate-posterior-pair interval is instead an internal relaxation obtained by dropping only the shared-pair constraint, and the complete rational transcript proves a strict open-set gap against it.  Masten and Poirier \cite{MastenPoirier2020BreakdownFrontier} motivate the tipping frontier, Fang and Santos \cite{FangSantos2019InferenceDirectional} motivate nonsmooth inference, and Manski \cite{Manski1990TreatmentResponse} is recovered only in the joint infinite-budget limit with vanishing latent positivity.
technical_internal_limitation: The one-arc theorem removes two-dimensional interior searches and duplicate forward-arc enumeration, and it also proves that finite-budget endpoints are attained in the strictly positive class.  The worked rational witness is fully certified by the explicit \((\mathrm{C1})\)--\((\mathrm{C10})\) polynomial, Sturm, interval-Newton, legal-cell, and competitor transcript.  The fixed-input certificate and parametric atlas remain exact mathematical procedures rather than complexity guarantees for a software implementation.  The regular inference theorem is pointwise and applies only to a unique nondegenerate active branch with nonzero budget gradient; uniformly honest Hausdorff inference at ties, legal-root collisions, stationary continua, and contact order \(k\geq2\) remains open.  No historical class transfer, nesting assertion, or numerical-dominance comparison with a published sensitivity model is claimed absent a proved observable-law-dependent translation.
honest_scope: The sharp population result concerns the maintained single-binary-confounder class with finite categorical \(X\), interior observed cells, and finite odds budgets.  Its causal image is identical over the strictly positive class and its explicitly defined finite-simplex closure: \(\tau(\mathcal M^{\circ})=\tau(\mathcal M)=[L,R]\).  Every nontrivial stratum endpoint lies at \(0<t<1\) on the canonical reverse exposure arc, with the forward arc recovered by complementing \(U\); \(\Gamma_A=1\) and \(\Gamma_0=\Gamma_1=1\) are point-identified and admit the strictly positive pair \(w_0=w_1=1/2\).  The odds ratio is not assigned a value at null cells.  The \((\mathrm{C1})\)--\((\mathrm{C10})\) transcript establishes the displayed common-versus-separate witness and its open-neighborhood strictness.  The zero-tipping surface has a parametric algebraic atlas, and unique regular branches have pointwise root-\(n\) normal-displacement inference; the open question is restricted to uniform inference on singular frontier strata.  Manski recovery is only the joint all-budget limit along vanishing latent treatment positivity.  Rosenbaum--Rubin remains a fixed-tuple comparator.  Without a proved observable-law-dependent translation, no nesting or numerical-dominance relation with a published model is asserted.

definitions.name: Strictly positive common-binary-confounder class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M^{\circ}(P_{\mathrm{obs}},\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)=\{\widetilde P\in\Delta_{\mathrm{full}}^{\circ}:\mathcal L_{\widetilde P}(X,A,Y)=P_{\mathrm{obs}},\;Y=AY(1)+(1-A)Y(0)\text{ almost surely},\;(Y(0),Y(1))\perp A\mid(X,U),\;\zeta_{1,1,x}\zeta_{0,0,x}\leq\Gamma_A\zeta_{1,0,x}\zeta_{0,1,x},\;\zeta_{1,0,x}\zeta_{0,1,x}\leq\Gamma_A\zeta_{1,1,x}\zeta_{0,0,x}\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal X,\;\eta_{a,1,1,x}\eta_{a,0,0,x}\leq\Gamma_a\eta_{a,1,0,x}\eta_{a,0,1,x},\;\eta_{a,1,0,x}\eta_{a,0,1,x}\leq\Gamma_a\eta_{a,1,1,x}\eta_{a,0,0,x}\text{ for every }(a,x)\in\{0,1\}\times\mathcal X\}\).

definitions.name: Feasible binary-mixture root
definitions.construction: Let \(B=1+(w-r)(\theta-1)\).  Define \(\kappa(r,w,\theta)=r\) when \(\theta=1\), and \(\kappa(r,w,\theta)=2r/\{B+\sqrt{B^2+4(1-w)(\theta-1)r}\}\) when \(\theta\neq1\), with the continuous value used at removable cases.

definitions.name: Common-pair endpoint functionals
definitions.construction: Define \(q^-_{a,x}(w_0,w_1)=\min_{\theta\in\{\Gamma_a^{-1},\Gamma_a\}}q_{a,x}(w_0,w_1;\theta)\) and \(q^+_{a,x}(w_0,w_1)=\max_{\theta\in\{\Gamma_a^{-1},\Gamma_a\}}q_{a,x}(w_0,w_1;\theta)\).  Set \(H^-_x=q^-_{1,x}-q^+_{0,x}\), \(H^+_x=q^+_{1,x}-q^-_{0,x}\), \(\ell_x=\min_{D_{A,x}}H^-_x\), \(\upsilon_x=\max_{D_{A,x}}H^+_x\), \(L=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\lambda_x\ell_x\), and \(R=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\lambda_x\upsilon_x\).

definitions.name: Internal separate-posterior-pair outer relaxation
definitions.construction: \(L_{\mathrm{sep}}=\sum_x\lambda_x\{\min_{D_{A,x}}q^-_{1,x}-\max_{D_{A,x}}q^+_{0,x}\}\) and \(R_{\mathrm{sep}}=\sum_x\lambda_x\{\max_{D_{A,x}}q^+_{1,x}-\min_{D_{A,x}}q^-_{0,x}\}\), where the two extrema within braces may use different posterior pairs; \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{sep}}=[L_{\mathrm{sep}},R_{\mathrm{sep}}]\).  This is an internal outer relaxation of the common-binary-confounder class, not a published marginal-sensitivity model.

definitions.name: Degeneracy-aware one-arc semialgebraic certificate
definitions.construction: For fixed rational observed summaries and rational finite budgets, \(\mathsf{CERT}\) first treats \(\Gamma_A=1\) and \(\Gamma_0=\Gamma_1=1\) as the point-identified cases.  Otherwise it sets \(W_{\Gamma_A}(t)=\Gamma_A t/\{1+(\Gamma_A-1)t\}\) and evaluates only the canonical reverse-arc objectives \(H_x^-(W_{\Gamma_A}(t),t)\) and \(H_x^+(W_{\Gamma_A}(t),t)\) for \(t\in[0,1]\); the forward arc is represented by complementing \(U\) and is not enumerated separately.  The procedure treats each \(\Gamma_a=1\) branch separately, adjoins the legal quadratic-root variables for nontrivial arms, evaluates \(t=0,1\) as the constant-\(U\) corners, saturates every stationary ideal by all cleared denominators, legal-root derivatives, and branch-boundary polynomials, isolates generic zero-dimensional stationary candidates by iterated resultants and Sturm sequences, and validates every isolated candidate against the original equations and inequalities by rational interval Newton tests.  An identically vanishing resultant, a legal-root collision, or a positive-dimensional stationary continuum is passed to cylindrical algebraic decomposition rather than discarded.  For the fixed input, \(\mathsf{CERT}\) returns real-algebraic endpoint values, rational isolating intervals, and exact membership certificates; it does not return a symbolic atlas over varying inputs.

definitions.name: Canonical-arc parametric cylindrical-algebraic atlas procedure
definitions.construction: For rational or real-algebraic observed summaries and endpoints of \(\mathcal B\), \(\mathsf{ATLAS}\) treats \((\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\in\mathcal B\) as parameters.  It separates the point-identified strata \(\Gamma_A=1\) and \(\Gamma_0=\Gamma_1=1\); on every remaining stratum it sets \(W_{\Gamma_A}(t)=\Gamma_A t/\{1+(\Gamma_A-1)t\}\), represents the forward exposure arc by the complement involution on \(U\), and constructs the lower and upper objectives only on the canonical arc \((w_0,w_1)=(W_{\Gamma_A}(t),t)\).  It then eliminates the legal mixture-root and one-dimensional stationary variables, including all saturated denominator and endpoint cases, and performs parametric cylindrical algebraic decomposition over \(K_{\mathrm{in}}\).  The output consists of exact quantifier-free sign cells and algebraic optimizer strata, including legal-root collisions and stationary continua; rational isolating intervals are returned only after a zero-dimensional specialization.

definitions.name: Rational common-confounder witness
definitions.construction: In one stratum, \(P^\star\) has \(p=1/2\), \(w_1=4/5\), \(w_0=1/5\), \((\mu_{1,1},\mu_{1,0})=(13/20,1/20)\), \((\mu_{0,1},\mu_{0,0})=(4/5,1/10)\), and \((\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)=(16,36,36)\).  Conditional on \((X,U)\), draw \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) as independent Bernoulli variables with these risks, and draw \(A\) from the Bayes-compatible Bernoulli law determined by \(p,w_0,w_1\).  Direct substitution gives the exact feasibility identities \(r_1=(4/5)(13/20)+(1/5)(1/20)=53/100\), \(r_0=(1/5)(4/5)+(4/5)(1/10)=6/25\), \(\pi=1/2\), \(\operatorname{OR}(w_1,w_0)=16\), \(\operatorname{OR}(13/20,1/20)=247/7<36\), and \(\operatorname{OR}(4/5,1/10)=36\).  All eight conditional Bernoulli cell probabilities are strictly between zero and one, and \(\tau(P^\star)=\{(13/20+1/20)-(4/5+1/10)\}/2=-1/10\).

definitions.name: Regular-branch and singular-frontier inference handle
definitions.construction:
Let \(b=(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_{J-1},(p_x,r_{0,x},r_{1,x})_{x\in\mathcal X})\) be a nonredundant observed-summary chart and let \(\gamma=(\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\).  The handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{inf}}\) takes an asymptotically linear estimator \(\widehat b_n\), the legal active equations \(F(z,b,\gamma)=0\) and objective \(\phi(z,b,\gamma)\) used by \(\mathsf{CERT}\) or selected on a stratum of \(\mathsf{ATLAS}\), and a covariance estimator.  On a unique legal branch with invertible \(F_z\), nonzero denominators, strict inactive inequalities, strict objective separation, and \(\nabla_\gamma L\neq0\), it computes
\[
\dot L_b=\phi_b-\phi_zF_z^{-1}F_b,
\qquad
\dot L_\gamma=\phi_\gamma-\phi_zF_z^{-1}F_\gamma,
\qquad
\sigma_L^2=\dot L_b\Sigma\dot L_b^{\mathsf T},
\]
and reports the pointwise normal-displacement standard-error constant \(\sigma_L/\|\dot L_\gamma\|\); it applies the analogous formulas to \(R\).  At a finite tie it records the minimum, or maximum, of the tied branch derivatives as the pointwise directional derivative.  At a legal-root collision, positive-dimensional stationary set, or higher-order contact, the handle returns the relevant \(\mathsf{ATLAS}\) cell, legal active equations, and algebraic germ data without applying the regular normal-coordinate inversion.

statements.statement: For every \(r\in(0,1)\), \(w\in[0,1]\), and \(\theta>0\), the equation \((1-w)(\theta-1)m_0^2+[1+(w-r)(\theta-1)]m_0-r=0\) has exactly one feasible root \(m_0\in(0,1)\), namely \(m_0=\kappa(r,w,\theta)\); with \(m_1=\theta m_0/\{1+(\theta-1)m_0\}\), it uniquely solves \(r=(1-w)m_0+wm_1\).
statements.justification: This isolates the unique legal branch and prevents denominator-clearing artifacts from entering the global program.
statements.gap: Rosenbaum--Rubin derive the corresponding fixed-parameter positive root; the present lemma records the probability-scale root including removable and boundary cases needed by an exact optimizer.
statements.consumer: The endpoint certificate uses this root to reject every algebraic candidate that lies on the wrong mixture branch.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(r\in(0,1)\), \(w\in[0,1]\), and \(\theta>0\).  Put
\[
T_\theta(z)=\frac{\theta z}{1+(\theta-1)z},\qquad
f_\theta(z)=(1-w)z+wT_\theta(z),\qquad 0\leq z\leq1.
\]
The denominator in \(T_\theta\) is \(1-z+\theta z>0\), and
\[
T_\theta'(z)=\frac{\theta}{\{1+(\theta-1)z\}^2}>0,\qquad
f_\theta'(z)=(1-w)+wT_\theta'(z)>0.
\]
Moreover, \(f_\theta(0)=0\) and \(f_\theta(1)=1\).  The intermediate-value theorem and strict monotonicity therefore give exactly one \(m_0\in(0,1)\) such that \(f_\theta(m_0)=r\), and then \(m_1=T_\theta(m_0)\in(0,1)\) is unique.

Multiplication by the strictly positive denominator \(1+(\theta-1)m_0\) gives, without introducing an extraneous solution,
\[
(1-w)(\theta-1)m_0^2+\bigl[1+(w-r)(\theta-1)\bigr]m_0-r=0.
\]
Write \(B=1+(w-r)(\theta-1)\) and \(D=B^2+4(1-w)(\theta-1)r\).  If \(\theta=1\), the displayed equation is \(m_0-r=0\).  If \(\theta\neq1\), the unique feasible root, including the linear case \(w=1\), is
\[
m_0=\frac{2r}{B+\sqrt D}.
\]
Indeed, when \(w<1\) this is the quadratic root obtained by rationalizing \((-B+\sqrt D)/\{2(1-w)(\theta-1)\}\), and uniqueness of the root in \((0,1)\) selects its nonnegative square root.  Its denominator is positive: for \(\theta>1\) and \(w<1\), \(D>B^2\); for \(\theta<1\), \(B=1-(w-r)(1-\theta)>0\); and for \(w=1\), \(B=r+(1-r)\theta>0\) and \(D=B^2\).  Thus this root is exactly \(\kappa(r,w,\theta)\) from Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}mixture\text{-}root}\), including its removable value at \(\theta=1\), and the claimed mixture identity follows from \(f_\theta(m_0)=r\).

statements.statement: On the strictly positive outcome chart, for fixed \((r,w,\pi)\), \(m_1-m_0\) is strictly increasing in \(\theta\), and \(q-r=(\pi-w)(m_1-m_0)\).  Hence the extrema over \(\theta\in[\Gamma_a^{-1},\Gamma_a]\) occur at \(\theta\in\{\Gamma_a^{-1},\Gamma_a\}\): if \(\pi-w\geq0\), the lower and upper choices are \(\Gamma_a^{-1}\) and \(\Gamma_a\), while the choices reverse if \(\pi-w\leq0\).
statements.justification: The lemma reduces a continuum of outcome-association choices to two analytic sign branches.
statements.gap: VanderWeele--Arah expose the same bias product, but do not prove endpoint reduction under two-sided odds budgets and a shared posterior pair.
statements.consumer: Applied sensitivity software needs only evaluate the two calibrated outcome-odds endpoints in each branch.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix an arm and stratum and suppress those indices.  By Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}mixture\text{-}inversion}\), write \(m_0=\operatorname{expit}(s)\), \(m_1=\operatorname{expit}(s+t)\), and \(t=\log\theta\), where \(s\) is uniquely chosen so that
\[
r=(1-w)m_0+wm_1.
\]
Let \(v_j=m_j(1-m_j)>0\).  Differentiation at fixed \(r\) is legitimate because \((1-w)v_0+wv_1>0\), and gives
\[
0=\{(1-w)v_0+wv_1\}\frac{ds}{dt}+wv_1,
\qquad
\frac{ds}{dt}=-\frac{wv_1}{(1-w)v_0+wv_1}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\frac{d(m_1-m_0)}{dt}
=v_1\left(1+\frac{ds}{dt}\right)-v_0\frac{ds}{dt}
=\frac{v_0v_1}{(1-w)v_0+wv_1}>0.
\]
This calculation also covers \(w=0\) and \(w=1\).  Since \(dt/d\theta=1/\theta>0\), \(m_1-m_0\) is strictly increasing in \(\theta\).

On the positive chart, the outcome joint-cell cross-product ratio is
\[
\frac{\eta_{a,1,1,x}\eta_{a,0,0,x}}
     {\eta_{a,1,0,x}\eta_{a,0,1,x}}
=\frac{m_1(1-m_0)}{m_0(1-m_1)}=\theta,
\]
because the positive factors \(\widetilde P(U=u,X=x)\) cancel.  Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}outcome\text{-}odds\text{-}upper}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}outcome\text{-}odds\text{-}lower}\) are therefore exactly \(\Gamma_a^{-1}\leq\theta\leq\Gamma_a\).

Finally, the observed arm mixture and the marginal-\(U\) mixture are respectively
\[
r=(1-w)m_0+wm_1,
\qquad
q=(1-\pi)m_0+\pi m_1.
\]
Subtracting yields
\[
q-r=(\pi-w)(m_1-m_0).
\]
Thus \(q\) is increasing in \(\theta\) when \(\pi-w>0\), decreasing when \(\pi-w<0\), and constant when \(\pi=w\).  Its minimum and maximum over the closed odds-budget interval are consequently attained at \(\Gamma_a^{-1}\) and \(\Gamma_a\), in the order stated in the lemma; equality in the sign condition merely makes either endpoint an admissible choice.

statements.statement: The map \(\operatorname{OR}:(0,1)^2\to(0,\infty)\) has no path-independent continuous extension at \((0,0)\) or \((1,1)\), so \(\theta_{a,x}\) is used only on the strictly positive chart \(\mathcal M^{\circ}\).  For each \(r\in(0,1)\) and finite \(\theta>0\), \(\kappa(r,w,\theta)\), \(q_{a,x}(w_0,w_1;\theta)\), and the endpoint objectives \(H_x^-\) and \(H_x^+\) extend continuously in \((w_0,w_1)\) to all of the compact region \(D_{A,x}\), including the constant-\(U\) corners.
statements.justification: This separates the interior odds-ratio chart from the compact probability-scale optimization that attains boundary endpoints.
statements.gap: Fixed-parameter binary-confounder calculations do not distinguish the odds-ratio chart from its well-defined probability-scale boundary objectives.
statements.consumer: The sharpness theorem and exact verifier can include null latent cells without assigning an ill-defined boundary odds ratio.
statements.proof_tex:
For any fixed \(c>0\), as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\),
\[
\operatorname{OR}(c\varepsilon,\varepsilon)
=\frac{c(1-\varepsilon)}{1-c\varepsilon}\longrightarrow c.
\]
Distinct values of \(c\) give distinct limits at \((0,0)\).  Likewise,
\[
\operatorname{OR}(1-c\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon)
=\frac{1-c\varepsilon}{c(1-\varepsilon)}\longrightarrow c^{-1},
\]
so no path-independent continuous extension exists at \((1,1)\).  Hence the odds-ratio coordinate \(\theta_{a,x}\) is properly confined to \(\mathcal M^\circ\).

For fixed \(r\in(0,1)\) and finite \(\theta>0\), the proof of Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}mixture\text{-}inversion}\) represents \(\kappa(r,w,\theta)\) as the unique inverse of the continuous, strictly increasing map \(f_\theta\).  Its displayed radical formula has positive denominator also at \(w=0,1\), and therefore is continuous in \(w\in[0,1]\); the value at \(\theta=1\) is its removable limit \(r\).  It follows from Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}adjusted\text{-}arm\text{-}mean}\) that \(q_{a,x}(w_0,w_1;\theta)\) is continuous on \([0,1]^2\), because \(\pi_x=p_xw_1+(1-p_x)w_0\) is affine and every displayed denominator is positive.

The region \(D_{A,x}\) is the intersection of \([0,1]^2\) with two inverse images of \(({-}\infty,0]\) under polynomials, hence it is closed and compact.  A minimum or maximum of two continuous functions is continuous, since
\[
\min(f,g)=\frac{f+g-|f-g|}{2},
\qquad
\max(f,g)=\frac{f+g+|f-g|}{2}.
\]
Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}common\text{-}u\text{-}endpoints}\) and Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}outcome\text{-}budget\text{-}extrema}\) now imply that \(q^-_{a,x}\), \(q^+_{a,x}\), \(H_x^-\), and \(H_x^+\) extend continuously to all of \(D_{A,x}\).  At a constant-confounder corner \((w_0,w_1)=(c,c)\), with \(c\in\{0,1\}\), one has \(\pi_x=w_{a,x}=c\), so the identity
\[
q_{a,x}-r_{a,x}=(\pi_x-w_{a,x})(m_1-m_0)
\]
gives \(q_{a,x}=r_{a,x}\) for every finite \(\theta\).  Thus the compact probability-scale objective is well defined at precisely the corners where the odds-ratio chart itself is not.

statements.statement: The interior class \(\mathcal M^{\circ}(P_{\mathrm{obs}},\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\) equals the union of the strictly positive binary-logistic full-data coordinate families whose treatment coefficient obeys \(|\alpha_x|\leq\log\Gamma_A\) and whose arm-specific outcome coefficients obey \(|\delta_{a,x}|\leq\log\Gamma_a\), with intercepts varying freely subject to the observed margin.  Its closure \(\mathcal M\) is exactly the set of compatible laws in \(\Delta_{\mathrm{full}}\) satisfying the closed joint-cell inequalities in \(\zeta\) and \(\eta\); no conditional odds ratio is evaluated at a null cell.  This is an internal coordinate equivalence for the maintained class, not a claim of equality or inclusion with the historical class in Rosenbaum--Rubin Sections 2--4.
statements.proof_tex:
Throughout, \(1\leq\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1<\infty\), as required by the declared parameter spaces.  Write \(V=(Y(0),Y(1))\), and define \(\operatorname{logit}(s)=\log\{s/(1-s)\}\) for \(0<s<1\).

First let \(\widetilde P\in\mathcal M^{\circ}(P_{\mathrm{obs}},\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\).  Strict positivity in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}positive\text{-}common\text{-}u\text{-}class}\) makes every conditional probability below an element of \((0,1)\).  Define
\[
e_{u,x}=\widetilde P(A=1\mid U=u,X=x),
\qquad
b_x=\operatorname{logit}(e_{0,x}),
\]
and
\[
\alpha_x=\operatorname{logit}(e_{1,x})-
          \operatorname{logit}(e_{0,x}).
\]
Because \(u\in\{0,1\}\), these definitions give the binary-logistic coordinate identity
\[
\operatorname{logit}\widetilde P(A=1\mid U=u,X=x)
=b_x+\alpha_xu.                                           \tag{1}
\]
Put \(s_{u,x}=\widetilde P(U=u,X=x)>0\).  Then the definition of \(\zeta\) gives
\[
\zeta_{1,u,x}=s_{u,x}e_{u,x},
\qquad
\zeta_{0,u,x}=s_{u,x}(1-e_{u,x}).                         \tag{2}
\]
Cancelling the positive factor \(s_{0,x}s_{1,x}\) in (2) yields
\[
\frac{\zeta_{1,1,x}\zeta_{0,0,x}}
     {\zeta_{1,0,x}\zeta_{0,1,x}}
=\frac{e_{1,x}(1-e_{0,x})}{e_{0,x}(1-e_{1,x})}
=\exp(\alpha_x).                                          \tag{3}
\]
Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}treatment\text{-}odds\text{-}upper}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}treatment\text{-}odds\text{-}lower}\), together with positivity of the denominator in (3), are therefore equivalent to
\[
\Gamma_A^{-1}\leq\exp(\alpha_x)\leq\Gamma_A,
\]
and monotonicity of the logarithm makes this equivalent to
\[
|\alpha_x|\leq\log\Gamma_A.                              \tag{4}
\]

For the outcome coordinates, use the declared risks
\(\mu_{a,u,x}=\widetilde P\{Y(a)=1\mid U=u,X=x\}\) and define
\[
c_{a,x}=\operatorname{logit}(\mu_{a,0,x}),
\qquad
\delta_{a,x}=\operatorname{logit}(\mu_{a,1,x})-
              \operatorname{logit}(\mu_{a,0,x}).
\]
Again because \(u\) is binary,
\[
\operatorname{logit}\widetilde P\{Y(a)=1\mid U=u,X=x\}
=c_{a,x}+\delta_{a,x}u.                                   \tag{5}
\]
The definition of \(\eta\) gives
\[
\eta_{a,1,u,x}=s_{u,x}\mu_{a,u,x},
\qquad
\eta_{a,0,u,x}=s_{u,x}(1-\mu_{a,u,x}).                   \tag{6}
\]
Cancelling \(s_{0,x}s_{1,x}>0\) in (6) gives
\[
\frac{\eta_{a,1,1,x}\eta_{a,0,0,x}}
     {\eta_{a,1,0,x}\eta_{a,0,1,x}}
=\frac{\mu_{a,1,x}(1-\mu_{a,0,x})}
       {\mu_{a,0,x}(1-\mu_{a,1,x})}
=\exp(\delta_{a,x}).                                     \tag{7}
\]
Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}outcome\text{-}odds\text{-}upper}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}outcome\text{-}odds\text{-}lower}\) are consequently equivalent, on the positive chart, to
\[
|\delta_{a,x}|\leq\log\Gamma_a.                          \tag{8}
\]

Conversely, suppose a strictly positive full-data law satisfies the observed-margin, consistency, and latent-ignorability conditions in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}positive\text{-}common\text{-}u\text{-}class}\), and admits (1) and (5) with (4) and (8).  Reversing (3) and (7) proves all four weak cross-product inequalities in that definition.  The law therefore belongs to \(\mathcal M^{\circ}\).  The two implications prove the asserted union equality.  The intercepts \(b_x\) and \(c_{a,x}\) may range over \(\mathbb R\), subject only to the requirement that, together with the law of \((X,U)\) and a strictly positive conditional coupling of \(V\), the resulting law obey the fixed observed margin.  Thus this is an internal reparameterization of the maintained class.

We next prove the closure assertion without assigning an odds ratio at a null cell.  Let \(C\subseteq\Delta_{\mathrm{full}}\) be the set of nonnegative full-data tables satisfying the observed-margin and consistency restrictions, the following division-free form of latent ignorability,
\[
\widetilde P(v,a,u,x)\widetilde P(u,x)
=\widetilde P(v,u,x)\widetilde P(a,u,x)                  \tag{9}
\]
for every \(v\in\{0,1\}^2\), \(a,u\in\{0,1\}\), and \(x\in\mathcal X\), and the four declared weak joint-cell inequalities in \(\zeta\) and \(\eta\).  Here the observed-margin and consistency restrictions state that the pushforward under
\[
(x,a,u,y_0,y_1)\longmapsto(x,a,ay_1+(1-a)y_0)
\]
equals \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\).  These pushforward restrictions are linear equalities in the full-table cells, (9) is a finite family of polynomial equalities, and the inequalities in \(\zeta\) and \(\eta\) are polynomial weak inequalities because \(\zeta\) and \(\eta\) are linear marginalizations of the full table.  Hence \(C\) is closed in the finite-dimensional simplex.  Every law in \(\mathcal M^{\circ}\) lies in \(C\), so Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}common\text{-}u\text{-}class}\) gives
\[
\mathcal M
=\operatorname{cl}_{\Delta_{\mathrm{full}}}\mathcal M^{\circ}
\subseteq C.                                              \tag{10}
\]

For the reverse inclusion, fix \(\widetilde P\in C\).  We construct strictly positive laws in the maintained class converging cellwise to \(\widetilde P\).  Fix \(x\in\mathcal X\).  By the declared support conditions, \(\lambda_x>0\), \(0<p_x<1\), and \(0<r_{a,x}<1\).  Thus
\[
w_{a,x}=\widetilde P(U=1\mid A=a,X=x)
\]
is well defined, and the treatment cells are
\[
\begin{aligned}
\zeta_{1,1,x}&=\lambda_xp_xw_{1,x},
&\zeta_{1,0,x}&=\lambda_xp_x(1-w_{1,x}),\\
\zeta_{0,1,x}&=\lambda_x(1-p_x)w_{0,x},
&\zeta_{0,0,x}&=\lambda_x(1-p_x)(1-w_{0,x}).
\end{aligned}                                             \tag{11}
\]
Cancelling \(\lambda_x^2p_x(1-p_x)>0\) in the two treatment inequalities gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
w_{1,x}(1-w_{0,x})
&\leq\Gamma_Aw_{0,x}(1-w_{1,x}),\\
w_{0,x}(1-w_{1,x})
&\leq\Gamma_Aw_{1,x}(1-w_{0,x}).
\end{aligned}                                             \tag{12}
\]
Because \(\Gamma_A<\infty\), (12) implies the exhaustive alternative
\[
0<w_{0,x},w_{1,x}<1,
\qquad (w_{0,x},w_{1,x})=(0,0),
\qquad\text{or}\qquad(w_{0,x},w_{1,x})=(1,1).            \tag{13}
\]
Indeed, setting either coordinate equal to zero in the inequality having the other coordinate on its left forces both to be zero; setting either coordinate equal to one in the other inequality forces both to be one.  All remaining pairs are interior.

Consider first the interior case in (13).  Both values of \(U\) then have positive probability given \(X=x\), and every \((A,U,X=x)\)-cell is positive.  Equation (9) implies that the conditional table
\[
g_{u,x}(y_0,y_1)
=\widetilde P\{V=(y_0,y_1)\mid U=u,X=x\}
\]
is also the conditional table of \(V\) given \((A=a,U=u,X=x)\), for either \(a\).  Define its armwise marginals by
\[
\mu_{a,u,x}=\sum_{y_0,y_1}y_a g_{u,x}(y_0,y_1).
\]
Consistency, the observed-margin restriction, and (9) imply
\[
r_{a,x}=(1-w_{a,x})\mu_{a,0,x}+w_{a,x}\mu_{a,1,x}.       \tag{14}
\]
Writing \(\rho_{u,x}=\widetilde P(U=u\mid X=x)>0\), the outcome cells are
\[
\eta_{a,1,u,x}=\lambda_x\rho_{u,x}\mu_{a,u,x},
\qquad
\eta_{a,0,u,x}=\lambda_x\rho_{u,x}(1-\mu_{a,u,x}).      \tag{15}
\]
After cancelling \(\lambda_x^2\rho_{0,x}\rho_{1,x}>0\), the two outcome inequalities become
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mu_{a,1,x}(1-\mu_{a,0,x})
&\leq\Gamma_a\mu_{a,0,x}(1-\mu_{a,1,x}),\\
\mu_{a,0,x}(1-\mu_{a,1,x})
&\leq\Gamma_a\mu_{a,1,x}(1-\mu_{a,0,x}).
\end{aligned}                                             \tag{16}
\]
Equations (14)--(16) and \(0<r_{a,x}<1\) imply
\[
0<\mu_{a,0,x},\mu_{a,1,x}<1.                             \tag{17}
\]
To verify the lower inequalities in (17), if either risk in (16) were zero, the inequality with the other risk on its left would force that other risk to be zero, contradicting (14).  For the upper inequalities, if either risk were one, the inequality with the complementary factor on its right would force the other risk to be one, again contradicting (14).

Let \(h_{u,x}\) be the product-Bernoulli table having the same two marginals as \(g_{u,x}\):
\[
h_{u,x}(y_0,y_1)
=\prod_{a=0}^1
 \mu_{a,u,x}^{y_a}(1-\mu_{a,u,x})^{1-y_a}.               \tag{18}
\]
By (17), every cell of \(h_{u,x}\) is positive.  For \(0<\varepsilon<1\), set
\[
g_{u,x}^{(\varepsilon)}
=(1-\varepsilon)g_{u,x}+\varepsilon h_{u,x}.             \tag{19}
\]
This table is strictly positive and has the same two Bernoulli marginals as \(g_{u,x}\).  Keep the \((A,U,X)\)-table fixed and use \(g_{u,x}^{(\varepsilon)}\) as the conditional law of \(V\) for both treatment values.  This preserves (9), the observed binary outcome margins through (14), and every \(\zeta\)- and \(\eta\)-inequality through (11) and (15), while making every full-data cell in this stratum positive.

It remains to treat a constant-confounder case in (13); write its constant value as \(c\in\{0,1\}\).  Since both treatment arms have positive probability and (9) holds, there is a common conditional table
\[
g_{c,x}(y_0,y_1)
=\widetilde P\{V=(y_0,y_1)\mid U=c,X=x\},
\]
whose arm-\(a\) marginal equals \(r_{a,x}\), by consistency and the observed-margin restriction.  Let
\[
h_x(y_0,y_1)
=\prod_{a=0}^1 r_{a,x}^{y_a}(1-r_{a,x})^{1-y_a}.          \tag{20}
\]
Every cell of \(h_x\) is positive.  For \(0<\varepsilon<1/2\), define
\[
\widetilde P^{(\varepsilon)}(U=c\mid A=a,X=x)=1-\varepsilon,
\qquad
\widetilde P^{(\varepsilon)}(U=1-c\mid A=a,X=x)=\varepsilon, \tag{21}
\]
and set
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal L_{\widetilde P^{(\varepsilon)}}(V\mid U=c,X=x)
&=(1-\varepsilon)g_{c,x}+\varepsilon h_x,\\
\mathcal L_{\widetilde P^{(\varepsilon)}}(V\mid U=1-c,X=x)
&=h_x,
\end{aligned}                                             \tag{22}
\]
using each conditional law in (22) for both values of \(A\).  Equations (20)--(22) make every full-data cell positive and impose (9).  Both conditional tables in (22) have arm-\(a\) risk \(r_{a,x}\), so the observed margin is unchanged.  Equation (21) makes the treatment cross-product ratio equal to one, and equality of the armwise risks across the two values of \(U\) makes every outcome cross-product ratio equal to one.  Since each budget is at least one, all four weak inequalities hold.  Moreover, (21)--(22) converge cellwise to the original constant-\(U\) table as \(\varepsilon\downarrow0\).

Apply (19) in every interior stratum and (21)--(22) in every constant-\(U\) stratum.  Finiteness of \(\mathcal X\) lets these constructions be combined, with the masses \(\lambda_x\) and the \((A,X)\)-margin fixed, into one law \(\widetilde P^{(\varepsilon)}\).  The binary outcome risks \(r_{a,x}\), propensities \(p_x\), and stratum masses \(\lambda_x\) characterize the observed law, so the observed-margin restriction is exact.  Every full-data cell is positive, and the law satisfies consistency, latent ignorability, and the four declared odds inequalities.  Therefore
\[
\widetilde P^{(\varepsilon)}
\in\mathcal M^{\circ}(P_{\mathrm{obs}},\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1),
\qquad
\widetilde P^{(\varepsilon)}\longrightarrow\widetilde P
\quad\text{cellwise}.                                    \tag{23}
\]
Thus \(C\subseteq\operatorname{cl}_{\Delta_{\mathrm{full}}}\mathcal M^{\circ}=\mathcal M\).  Together with (10), this proves \(C=\mathcal M\).  Every boundary step used only polynomial equalities and weak joint-cell inequalities, so no conditional odds ratio was evaluated at a null cell.  Finally, because the argument compares no distinct historical model class, it establishes neither equality nor inclusion with any class considered in Rosenbaum--Rubin Sections 2--4, exactly as claimed.
statements.justification: This identifies the exact binary-logistic coordinates of the maintained bounded class without attributing that class to a historical source whose fixed-tuple analysis has different documented scope.
statements.gap: The internal bounded-union and probability-table closure equivalence must be proved independently; the cited Rosenbaum--Rubin sections support only fixed binary-confounder sensitivity recalculation, not equality or inclusion of classes.
statements.consumer: Readers can translate the maintained treatment and arm-specific outcome odds budgets into binary-logistic coordinates while keeping the historical comparison precise.

statements.statement:
For finite budgets and interior observed cells,
\[
 \{\tau(\widetilde P):\widetilde P\in\mathcal M^{\circ}(P_{\mathrm{obs}},\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\}
 =\{\tau(\widetilde P):\widetilde P\in\mathcal M(P_{\mathrm{obs}},\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\}
 =\mathcal I_{\mathrm{com}}=[L,R].
\]
The endpoints use one common \((w_{0,x},w_{1,x})\in D_{A,x}\) per stratum.  If \(\Gamma_A>1\) and \((\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\neq(1,1)\), every nontrivial stratum endpoint has a canonical-arc optimizer \((w_{0,x},w_{1,x})=(W_{\Gamma_A}(t),t)\) with \(0<t<1\); a forward-arc optimizer is its image under complementing \(U\).  If \(\Gamma_A=1\) or \(\Gamma_0=\Gamma_1=1\), both stratum endpoints equal \(r_{1,x}-r_{0,x}\) and are attained with the strictly positive pair \(w_{0,x}=w_{1,x}=1/2\).  For every selected pair, the endpoint-attaining law uses the feasible conditional Bernoulli potential-outcome marginals and may use any strictly positive coupling of them given \((X,U)\).  The result concerns only the maintained common-binary-confounder class and asserts no equality, inclusion, or numerical-dominance relation with the class in Rosenbaum--Rubin Sections 2--4.
statements.justification: This is the sharp population kernel: both potential-outcome arms are jointly realized through one latent confounder, strict tilt-gap monotonicity makes the endpoint map one-dimensional, and every endpoint is attained in the strictly positive class.
statements.gap: The fixed-tuple Rosenbaum--Rubin comparator, exposure-standardization procedures, and propensity-only marginal sensitivity bounds do not give the equality \(\tau(\mathcal M^{\circ})=\tau(\mathcal M)=[L,R]\) or its canonical-arc reduction.  No class relation is asserted without a proved observable-law-dependent translation.
statements.consumer: Investigators receive the narrowest valid ATE interval under the declared common-confounder budgets, strictly positive endpoint witnesses, and a one-dimensional map that exact certification and tipping analysis can consume.
statements.proof_tex:
Define the observed-law identified set
\[
 \Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}})
 =\{\tau(\widetilde P):
       \widetilde P\in\mathcal M(P_{\mathrm{obs}},\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\}.
                                                                            \tag{38}
\]
Here \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}=\mathcal L(X,A,Y)\) is a law on \(\mathcal X\times\{0,1\}^2\), \(\widetilde P\) is a law on \(\mathcal X\times\{0,1\}^4\), and \(\tau(\widetilde P)=\widetilde E\{Y(1)-Y(0)\}\).  We use the declared finite support, \(\lambda_x>0\), observed overlap \(0<p_x<1\), interior risks \(0<r_{a,x}<1\), and finite budgets \(1\leq\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1<\infty\).  These conditions justify conditioning and division and keep every finite tilt denominator positive.  No rank or matrix-inversion condition is used.

Fix \(x\in\mathcal X\) and first take \(\widetilde P\in\mathcal M^{\circ}\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}observed\text{-}margin}\) identifies \(\lambda_x,p_x,r_{a,x}\) with the full-law summaries.  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}consistency}\) gives
\[
 r_{a,x}=\widetilde P\{Y(a)=1\mid A=a,X=x\}.
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}latent\text{-}ignorability}\), followed by conditioning on binary \(U\), yields
\[
 r_{a,x}=(1-w_{a,x})\mu_{a,0,x}+w_{a,x}\mu_{a,1,x}.                    \tag{39}
\]
Bayes' rule is legal because every full-data cell is positive and gives
\[
 \pi_x=\widetilde P(U=1\mid X=x)
      =p_xw_{1,x}+(1-p_x)w_{0,x}.                                      \tag{40}
\]
The four positive \((A,U,X=x)\)-cell probabilities give
\[
 \frac{\zeta_{1,1,x}\zeta_{0,0,x}}
      {\zeta_{1,0,x}\zeta_{0,1,x}}
 =\frac{w_{1,x}(1-w_{0,x})}{w_{0,x}(1-w_{1,x})}.                       \tag{41}
\]
After cancellation of the positive factor \(\lambda_x^2p_x(1-p_x)\), Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}treatment\text{-}odds\text{-}upper}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}treatment\text{-}odds\text{-}lower}\) are exactly \((w_{0,x},w_{1,x})\in D_{A,x}\).

On the strictly positive chart, put \(\theta_{a,x}=\operatorname{OR}(\mu_{a,1,x},\mu_{a,0,x})\).  Cancelling the positive \((U,X=x)\)-margins in the two outcome cross products, Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}outcome\text{-}odds\text{-}upper}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}outcome\text{-}odds\text{-}lower}\) give
\[
 \Gamma_a^{-1}\leq\theta_{a,x}\leq\Gamma_a.                          \tag{42}
\]
Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}mixture\text{-}inversion}\) applied to (39) uniquely gives
\[
 \mu_{a,0,x}=\kappa(r_{a,x},w_{a,x},\theta_{a,x}),
 \qquad
 \mu_{a,1,x}
 =\frac{\theta_{a,x}\mu_{a,0,x}}
        {1+(\theta_{a,x}-1)\mu_{a,0,x}},                               \tag{43}
\]
with both risks strictly between zero and one.  Subtracting (39) from the marginal potential-outcome mean and using (40) gives the algebraic identity
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \widetilde E\{Y(a)\mid X=x\}
 &=(1-\pi_x)\mu_{a,0,x}+\pi_x\mu_{a,1,x}\\
 &=r_{a,x}+(\pi_x-w_{a,x})(\mu_{a,1,x}-\mu_{a,0,x})\\
 &=q_{a,x}(w_{0,x},w_{1,x};\theta_{a,x}).
\end{aligned}                                                           \tag{44}
\]
Thus the observed-law functional is linked to the causal mean by the assumptions; it has not been defined to equal it.

Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}outcome\text{-}budget\text{-}extrema}\) optimizes (44) over (42), separately in the two outcome arms but at the same posterior pair.  Hence
\[
 H_x^-(w_{0,x},w_{1,x})
 \leq \widetilde E\{Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X=x\}
 \leq H_x^+(w_{0,x},w_{1,x}),                                         \tag{45}
\]
and minimization or maximization over the common feasible pair gives
\[
 \ell_x\leq\widetilde E\{Y(1)-Y(0)\mid X=x\}\leq\upsilon_x.          \tag{46}
\]
After multiplication by \(\lambda_x>0\) and summation over the finite support,
\[
 L\leq\tau(\widetilde P)\leq R,
 \qquad \widetilde P\in\mathcal M^{\circ}.                            \tag{47}
\]
If \(\widetilde P\in\mathcal M\), Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}common\text{-}u\text{-}class}\) gives \(\widetilde P_k\in\mathcal M^{\circ}\) converging to \(\widetilde P\) in the finite simplex.  Since \(\tau\) is linear and continuous, (47) passes to the limit.  Therefore
\[
 \Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\subseteq[L,R].                             \tag{48}
\]

We construct compatible laws for the reverse inclusion.  In every stratum choose \((w_{0,x},w_{1,x})\in D_{A,x}\cap(0,1)^2\) and \(\theta_{a,x}\in[\Gamma_a^{-1},\Gamma_a]\), and set
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
 \widetilde P(A=1,U=1\mid X=x)=p_xw_{1,x},
 &\widetilde P(A=1,U=0\mid X=x)=p_x(1-w_{1,x}),\\
 \widetilde P(A=0,U=1\mid X=x)=(1-p_x)w_{0,x},
 &\widetilde P(A=0,U=0\mid X=x)=(1-p_x)(1-w_{0,x}).
\end{array}                                                             \tag{49}
\]
Observed overlap and interiority of the selected pair make all four probabilities positive.  Define \(\mu_{a,u,x}\) by (43).  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}mixture\text{-}inversion}\) puts them in \((0,1)\) and makes (39) hold.  Conditional on \((X=x,U=u)\), draw \(Y(0)\) and \(Y(1)\) independently as Bernoulli variables with success probabilities \(\mu_{0,u,x}\) and \(\mu_{1,u,x}\); draw \(A\) according to (49), independently of the potential outcomes given \((X,U)\); and set
\[
 Y=AY(1)+(1-A)Y(0).                                                     \tag{50}
\]
This construction proves \((Y(0),Y(1))\perp A\mid(X,U)\).  Equations (39), (49), and (50) reproduce the observed conditional law of \((A,Y)\).  Equation (41), membership in \(D_{A,x}\), and (42) verify all four odds restrictions.  With \(\widetilde P(X=x)=\lambda_x\), every full-data cell is positive, so the constructed law belongs to \(\mathcal M^{\circ}\), and (44) gives its causal means.

It remains to show that this interior construction attains every value in \([L,R]\), including its endpoints.  Define
\[
 \mathcal D_x^{\circ}
 =\{D_{A,x}\cap(0,1)^2\}
  \times[\Gamma_0^{-1},\Gamma_0]
  \times[\Gamma_1^{-1},\Gamma_1].                                    \tag{51}
\]
The coordinatewise logit map sends the posterior-pair factor bijectively to the convex strip
\[
 \{(s_0,s_1)\in\mathbb R^2:
      |s_1-s_0|\leq\log\Gamma_A\},                                    \tag{52}
\]
so that factor, and therefore \(\mathcal D_x^{\circ}\), is connected.  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}mixture\text{-}inversion}\) and Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}closed\text{-}chart\text{-}extension}\) make the stratum contrast continuous on (51).

Suppose first that \(\Gamma_A>1\) and \((\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\neq(1,1)\).  Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}one\text{-}arc\text{-}endpoint\text{-}reduction}\) gives canonical-arc optimizers over \(0\leq t\leq1\).  At \(t=0\) or \(t=1\), the pair is constant and both endpoint objectives equal \(r_{1,x}-r_{0,x}\).  For any \(0<t<1\), \(W_{\Gamma_A}(t)>t\).  The formulas and strict tilt-gap positivity in that theorem then give
\[
 H_x^+(W_{\Gamma_A}(t),t)>r_{1,x}-r_{0,x},
 \qquad
 H_x^-(W_{\Gamma_A}(t),t)<r_{1,x}-r_{0,x},                             \tag{53}
\]
because at least one of \(\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1\) exceeds one and \(p_x,1-p_x>0\).  Thus neither optimizer is an endpoint of the arc, and compactness supplies optimizing \(t\)'s with \(0<t<1\).  Their posterior pairs lie in (51), and Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}outcome\text{-}budget\text{-}extrema}\) supplies the endpoint tilts that attain \(\ell_x\) and \(\upsilon_x\).  If instead \(\Gamma_A=1\) or \(\Gamma_0=\Gamma_1=1\), the one-arc theorem gives \(\ell_x=\upsilon_x=r_{1,x}-r_{0,x}\); this value is attained in (51) by \(w_{0,x}=w_{1,x}=1/2\) and \(\theta_{0,x}=\theta_{1,x}=1\).

Therefore the continuous image of connected \(\mathcal D_x^{\circ}\) lies in \([\ell_x,\upsilon_x]\) by (45) and contains both endpoints, so it equals that interval.  The finite product \(\prod_x\mathcal D_x^{\circ}\) is connected, and the continuous weighted-sum map has image
\[
 \left[\sum_x\lambda_x\ell_x,
       \sum_x\lambda_x\upsilon_x\right]=[L,R].                       \tag{54}
\]
Applying (49)--(50) to every point in this product proves
\[
 [L,R]
 \subseteq\{\tau(\widetilde P):\widetilde P\in\mathcal M^{\circ}\}
 \subseteq\{\tau(\widetilde P):\widetilde P\in\mathcal M\}.
                                                                            \tag{55}
\]
Together with (48), this establishes
\[
 \{\tau(\widetilde P):\widetilde P\in\mathcal M^{\circ}\}
 =\{\tau(\widetilde P):\widetilde P\in\mathcal M\}
 =[L,R].                                                                 \tag{56}
\]
The endpoint laws constructed above use independent conditional Bernoulli potential outcomes.  More generally, any strictly positive coupling of the same two Bernoulli marginals given \((X,U)\) preserves every displayed calculation and conditional ignorability.  A coupling with zero cells belongs to the closed class after mixing it with an arbitrarily small amount of the independent coupling, which preserves the marginals and converges in the finite simplex.  This final closure observation concerns alternative couplings only; equation (56) shows that no endpoint requires a boundary posterior pair.  Rosenbaum--Rubin is used only as a historical fixed-tuple comparator, and no historical class equality, inclusion, or numerical dominance is used.

statements.statement: For fixed rational \((p_x,r_{0,x},r_{1,x},\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\) with interior observed cells and finite budgets, \(\mathsf{CERT}\) terminates and returns exact real-algebraic representations, rational isolating intervals, and exact membership certificates for \(\ell_x\) and \(\upsilon_x\).  Its endpoint candidate list is exhaustive: it enumerates every legal analytic outcome-sign branch on the canonical reverse exposure-odds arc and its endpoints, while the forward arc is represented exactly by complementing \(U\); the one-arc reduction rules out every two-dimensional interior optimizer.  It neither admits a cleared-denominator artifact nor omits a legal root, and it handles separately \(\Gamma_A=1\), each \(\Gamma_a=1\), constant-\(U\) corners, root collisions, identically vanishing resultants, and positive-dimensional stationary continua.  This fixed-input output is not a symbolic atlas over varying observed summaries or budgets.
statements.justification: An exact bound is operational only if every branch and degeneracy has a terminating, auditable certificate.
statements.gap: Existing binary-\(U\) analyses use user-selected grids, and modern marginal-sensitivity bounds use convex duality; neither supplies a complete verifier for this algebraic common-law program.
statements.consumer: A reproducible implementation can attach exact isolating intervals and branch witnesses to reported sensitivity endpoints.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a stratum \(x\) and suppress its subscript.  Thus \(p,r_0,r_1\in(0,1)\), the three budgets are finite rational numbers at least one, and every conditioning operation below is justified by observed overlap.  The proof uses exact semialgebraic graphing, the proved one-arc reduction, resultant elimination on zero-dimensional strata, signed-remainder root isolation, rational interval Newton validation, and sign-invariant cylindrical algebraic decomposition on exceptional strata.

For an arm \(a\), an endpoint \(\vartheta\in\{\Gamma_a^{-1},\Gamma_a\}\), and a new variable \(z_a\), put
\[
 F_a(w_a,z_a;\vartheta)
 =(1-w_a)(\vartheta-1)z_a^2
 +\{1+(w_a-r_a)(\vartheta-1)\}z_a-r_a
\]
and \(d_a=1+(\vartheta-1)z_a\).  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}mixture\text{-}inversion}\) proves that
\[
 F_a=0,\qquad 0<z_a<1,\qquad d_a>0                                      \tag{1}
\]
selects exactly one point, namely \(z_a=\kappa(r_a,w_a,\vartheta)\).  Thus adjoining \(z_a\) subject to (1) is an exact semialgebraic graph construction and introduces neither a missing branch nor a spurious quadratic root.  To record simplicity, define
\[
 G_a(z)=(1-w_a)z+w_a\frac{\vartheta z}{1+(\vartheta-1)z}-r_a.
\]
Since \(F_a=d_aG_a\), evaluation on (1) gives
\[
 \frac{\partial F_a}{\partial z_a}
 =d_a\left\{(1-w_a)+\frac{w_a\vartheta}{d_a^2}\right\}>0.              \tag{2}
\]
Every division and implicit differentiation below is therefore legal on the graph.  Moreover,
\[
 m_{a,0}=z_a,\qquad
 m_{a,1}=\frac{\vartheta z_a}{d_a},\qquad
 q_a=r_a+(\pi-w_a)(m_{a,1}-m_{a,0})                                    \tag{3}
\]
is rational with denominators of known positive sign.

We next expose all analytic outcome branches.  Since \(p\in(0,1)\),
\[
 \pi-w_1=(1-p)(w_0-w_1),
 \qquad
 \pi-w_0=p(w_1-w_0).                                                    \tag{4}
\]
Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}outcome\text{-}budget\text{-}extrema}\) applied to (3) yields the complete table
\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
 &H^-&H^+\\ \hline
 w_1>w_0&(\vartheta_1,\vartheta_0)=(\Gamma_1,\Gamma_0)
         &(\vartheta_1,\vartheta_0)=(\Gamma_1^{-1},\Gamma_0^{-1})\\
 w_1<w_0&(\vartheta_1,\vartheta_0)=(\Gamma_1^{-1},\Gamma_0^{-1})
         &(\vartheta_1,\vartheta_0)=(\Gamma_1,\Gamma_0).
\end{array}                                                             \tag{5}
\]
On \(w_0=w_1\), (4) gives
\[
 H^-=H^+=r_1-r_0.                                                       \tag{6}
\]
If \(\Gamma_a=1\), the two endpoint choices for that arm coincide and the arm contributes no root variable.  Thus (5)--(6), including equality faces, give finitely many and all legal analytic outcome-sign branches.

For \(\Gamma_A>1\), Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}one\text{-}arc\text{-}endpoint\text{-}reduction}\) gives
\[
 W_{\Gamma_A}(t)=\frac{\Gamma_A t}{1+(\Gamma_A-1)t},
 \qquad 0\leq t\leq1,                                                  \tag{7}
\]
and proves
\[
 \ell=\min_{0\leq t\leq1}H^-(W_{\Gamma_A}(t),t),
 \qquad
 \upsilon=\max_{0\leq t\leq1}H^+(W_{\Gamma_A}(t),t).                 \tag{8}
\]
The denominator in (7) is at least one.  The same theorem proves strict coordinate monotonicity on both two-dimensional sign cells, so no non-point-identified endpoint has a two-dimensional interior optimizer.  It also proves that complementing \(U\) maps every point of the forward exposure-odds arc to a point of the canonical reverse arc with the identical objective value.  Consequently (7), its two endpoints, and the finite branches (5) are exhaustive for both exposure arcs and for the global endpoint problem; there is no separate two-dimensional stationary system to enumerate.  At \(t=0,1\), the pairs are \((0,0)\) and \((1,1)\), and Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}closed\text{-}chart\text{-}extension}\) gives \(q_a=r_a\) without assigning an odds ratio at a null latent cell.  If \(\Gamma_A=1\), the two inequalities defining \(D_A\) imply \(w_0=w_1\); (6) then gives \(\ell=\upsilon=r_1-r_0\).  The same equality follows when \(\Gamma_0=\Gamma_1=1\).  These point-identified cases are evaluated directly.

Consider one nonconstant analytic branch after substituting (7), and write its rational objective as \(\Phi(t,z_0,z_1)\), constrained by \(F_0=F_1=0\); omit \(z_a\) whenever \(\Gamma_a=1\).  By (2), implicit differentiation is legal, and a tangential stationary point satisfies
\[
 F_0=F_1=0,
 \qquad
 \frac{\partial\Phi}{\partial t}
 -\sum_{a=0}^1
   \frac{\partial\Phi}{\partial z_a}
   \frac{\partial F_a/\partial t}{\partial F_a/\partial z_a}=0.        \tag{9}
\]
Multiplying by the positive factors in (1)--(3), (7), and (2) turns (9) into a polynomial system without changing its legal solutions.  The branch endpoints and every equality face have already been assigned separate cells.  Saturating the stationary ideal by the cleared mixture denominators, the arc denominator, the legal-root derivatives, and the strict branch-boundary polynomials removes only components on which the rational derivation is undefined or which belong to those separate lower-dimensional cells.  Because every saturated factor is nonzero on the current cell, saturation removes no legal point from that cell.

Suppose first that a saturated stationary system is zero-dimensional.  Successive resultants eliminate the legal root variables.  At each elimination \(\mathsf{CERT}\) separately records the vanishing leading-coefficient and subresultant cases.  Hence the elementary implication
\[
 \text{common finite zero}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\text{resultant zero} \tag{10}
\]
shows that no solution is lost.  Euclidean polynomial division terminates because degree strictly decreases.  Square-free factorization leaves finitely many real roots.  For every square-free univariate factor, the deterministic signed-remainder chain has constant sign variation away from its roots, and the variation drops by one at each simple root; therefore the difference of endpoint variations counts the roots in any rational interval.  Repeated rational bisection produces disjoint rational isolating intervals for every projected root.  Subresultant back-substitution and the inequalities (1) lift those intervals to all and only the real solutions of the original stationary system.

For a nonsingular lifted solution, rational interval Newton contraction gives a box mapped strictly into itself and thereby certifies a unique zero.  If projected roots collide or a lifted isolated solution is singular, gcd, square-free, subresultant, and Thom-sign data record the collision exactly; interval Newton flags rather than deletes it, and exact algebraic sign evaluation against the original equations and inequalities supplies its membership certificate.  In every case the original uncleared equations, positive-denominator conditions, legal-root inequalities, branch conditions, and \(0\leq t\leq1\) are checked.  Thus a wrong quadratic root or a cleared-denominator artifact is rejected.

If a resultant vanishes identically or the stationary ideal is positive-dimensional, \(\mathsf{CERT}\) invokes sign-invariant cylindrical algebraic decomposition of the finite polynomial family consisting of the original constraints, branch boundaries, derivative equations, and objective comparisons.  Termination follows by induction on the number of variables.  In one variable the signed-remainder isolation above produces finitely many points and intervals.  At each projection step, only finitely many coefficients, discriminants, and pairwise resultants are added.  On every lower-dimensional cell where those projection polynomials have fixed nonzero signs, degrees and multiplicities are fixed and distinct real roots cannot cross, so finitely many ordered sections and sectors lift the decomposition.  On a cell where a projection polynomial vanishes, specialization lowers a degree or records an equality and the same finite recursion applies.  The variable count falls at projection and every polynomial family remains finite.  Hence the recursion terminates and returns a stationary continuum or legal-root collision as an exact algebraic cell instead of discarding it.

Exhaustiveness is now immediate but we state it carefully.  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}closed\text{-}chart\text{-}extension}\) makes each objective continuous on the compact exposure region, so its extrema exist.  Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}one\text{-}arc\text{-}endpoint\text{-}reduction}\) places every non-point-identified optimizer on the canonical arc, up to the complement involution.  The finite stratification by (5)--(7) places it either at a listed zero-dimensional endpoint or in the relative interior of a one-dimensional analytic cell.  In the latter case its tangential derivative vanishes unless the objective is constant on the cell; isolated zeros are retained by the resultant branch and a nonisolated zero set is retained by cylindrical decomposition.  The point-identified strata were evaluated directly.  Thus every optimizer is represented by an enumerated algebraic point or cell.

Finally, algebraic objective values at distinct candidates are compared exactly by refining their rational isolating intervals until disjoint.  If two values coincide, reduction in their common algebraic coordinate ring certifies equality.  Exact sign evaluation supplies membership certificates for all original constraints.  Performing these finite operations for \(H^-\) and \(H^+\) returns exact real-algebraic representations, rational isolating intervals, and exact membership certificates for \(\ell_x\) and \(\upsilon_x\).  Repeating over the finite set \(\mathcal X\) proves the theorem.  All coefficients were specialized fixed rational inputs; no step returns a symbolic atlas over varying inputs.

statements.statement: Always \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{com}}\subseteq\mathcal I_{\mathrm{sep}}\), where \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{sep}}\) is the internal outer relaxation that permits the two arms to use different posterior pairs and is not a published marginal-sensitivity procedure.  For the observed law and budgets in \(P^\star\), the worked exact certificate \(\mathcal C^\star\) gives \(L\in[-107500302/10^9,-107500301/10^9]\), \(L_{\mathrm{sep}}=-3461701/31346200\in[-110434471/10^9,-110434470/10^9]\), \(R\in[539509967/10^9,539509968/10^9]\), and \(R_{\mathrm{sep}}=84380923/150997400\in[558823681/10^9,558823682/10^9]\).  Thus both endpoint inequalities are strict, and they remain strict on a relatively open neighborhood of the displayed interior observed law and finite budgets.  The attaining witness itself has \(r_1=53/100\), \(r_0=6/25\), \(\operatorname{OR}(A,U)=16\), \(\theta_1=247/7<36\), \(\theta_0=36\), \(\tau(P^\star)=-1/10\), and nominal contrast \(r_1-r_0=29/100\).
statements.justification: The strict open-set gap demonstrates that common-law compatibility has empirical content beyond a hand-picked numerical coincidence.
statements.gap: The internal armwise relaxation removes only common-posterior compatibility inside the present model.  No nesting or numerical-dominance relation with the Dorn--Guo marginal sensitivity model is asserted absent a proved observable-law-dependent translation; no published result isolates this shared-binary-posterior loss under simultaneous treatment and outcome odds budgets.
statements.consumer: Analysts avoid reporting materially overwide intervals that combine mutually incompatible armwise confounder distributions.
statements.proof_tex:
For a stratum \(x\), abbreviate a posterior pair by \(d\in D_{A,x}\).  For every such \(d\), elementary minimization and maximization give
\[
 q^-_{1,x}(d)-q^+_{0,x}(d)
 \geq \min_{e\in D_{A,x}}q^-_{1,x}(e)
      -\max_{f\in D_{A,x}}q^+_{0,x}(f).                                \tag{11}
\]
Taking the minimum of the left side, multiplying by \(\lambda_x>0\), and summing proves \(L\geq L_{\mathrm{sep}}\).  Similarly,
\[
 q^+_{1,x}(d)-q^-_{0,x}(d)
 \leq \max_{e\in D_{A,x}}q^+_{1,x}(e)
      -\min_{f\in D_{A,x}}q^-_{0,x}(f),                                \tag{12}
\]
so \(R\leq R_{\mathrm{sep}}\).  Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp\text{-}common\text{-}u\text{-}envelope}\) identifies the common-pair interval and Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}separate\text{-}pair\text{-}relaxation}\) defines the separate-pair outer relaxation.  Hence
\[
 L_{\mathrm{sep}}\leq L\leq R\leq R_{\mathrm{sep}},
 \qquad \mathcal I_{\mathrm{com}}\subseteq\mathcal I_{\mathrm{sep}}.  \tag{13}
\]

We verify the law in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}rational\text{-}witness}\).  Its marginal confounder prevalence and treatment odds ratio are
\[
 \pi=\frac12\frac45+\frac12\frac15=\frac12,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{OR}\!\left(\frac45,\frac15\right)=16.                 \tag{14}
\]
Its observed risks and outcome odds ratios are
\[
\begin{aligned}
 r_1&=\frac45\frac{13}{20}+\frac15\frac1{20}=\frac{53}{100},
 &\theta_1&=\frac{(13/20)(19/20)}{(1/20)(7/20)}=\frac{247}{7}<36,\\
 r_0&=\frac15\frac45+\frac45\frac1{10}=\frac6{25},
 &\theta_0&=\frac{(4/5)(9/10)}{(1/10)(1/5)}=36.
\end{aligned}                                                           \tag{15}
\]
Bayes' rule gives \(P^\star(A=1\mid U=1)=4/5\) and \(P^\star(A=1\mid U=0)=1/5\).  These probabilities and all four outcome risks are strictly between zero and one.  The conditional independent-Bernoulli construction in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}rational\text{-}witness}\) therefore makes every full-data cell positive and gives \((Y(0),Y(1))\perp A\mid U\).  Equations (14)--(15) verify the four sensitivity inequalities.  Thus \(P^\star\in\mathcal M^{\circ}\), and
\[
 \tau(P^\star)
 =\frac12\left(\frac{13}{20}+\frac1{20}-\frac45-\frac1{10}\right)
 =-\frac1{10},
 \qquad r_1-r_0=\frac{29}{100}.                                        \tag{16}
\]

It remains to validate the endpoint transcript rather than treating its construction as proof.  On the canonical reverse arc in (C8), \(w_0=W(t)>t=w_1\), and
\[
 w_0(1-w_1)=16w_1(1-w_0),
 \qquad
 16w_0(1-w_1)-w_1(1-w_0)=255w_1(1-w_0)>0.                              \tag{17}
\]
Since \(p=1/2\), \(\pi-w_1=(W-t)/2>0\) and \(\pi-w_0=(t-W)/2<0\).  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}outcome\text{-}budget\text{-}extrema}\) makes the common lower branch \(J_{1/36}\) and upper branch \(J_{36}\), exactly as recorded in (C1)--(C2).  Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}one\text{-}arc\text{-}endpoint\text{-}reduction}\) proves that neither common endpoint has a two-dimensional interior optimizer and that complementing \(U\) duplicates the forward-arc values.  Hence (C8) reduces the common optimization exhaustively to this one arc, its diagonal, and its constant-\(U\) endpoints.  The same theorem's strict derivative inequalities applied to a single adjustment term show that each separate armwise extremum also enlarges strictly with posterior separation, so its optimizer is on an exposure boundary; complementing \(U\) again reduces it to the canonical arc.

For the one-dimensional common candidates, (C2) is the numerator obtained by differentiating the two mixture equations along the arc.  Equation (2) in the proof of Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}complete\text{-}semialgebraic\text{-}certificate}\) shows that neither legal-root derivative vanishes.  Thus every legal stationary point must annul \(g_-(t)\) or \(g_+(t)\) in (C3)--(C4).  The deterministic Sturm recurrence specified before (C5), together with the variation differences \(8-6=2\), proves that each degree-sixteen polynomial has exactly two roots in \((0,1)\).  The four one-unit variation drops in (C5) isolate all four roots.  Substitution into the original three-equation systems, the nonzero Jacobian enclosures (C7), the legal-risk and denominator checks following (C7), and rational interval Newton contraction validate exactly one legal stationary triple in each box in (C6).  Thus no resultant root is missed, duplicated, or admitted through denominator clearing.

The diagonal and both corner objectives equal \(29/100\).  Comparing this value and all four objective enclosures in (C6) shows that the first lower row and the second upper row are the selected extrema and gives
\[
 L\in[-107500302/10^9,-107500301/10^9],
 \qquad
 R\in[539509967/10^9,539509968/10^9].                                  \tag{18}
\]
The complete-certificate theorem justifies the exact saturation, resultant, Sturm, interval-Newton, and membership operations, while the displayed (C1)--(C8) transcript supplies the complete fixed rational input, cell inventory, stationary polynomials, isolations, and competitor comparisons.

For the separate extrema, (C9) is obtained by the same exact implicit differentiation and elimination.  The extra resultant root \(t=9/325\) in \((0,1)\) forces \(z_0=414/395>1\) and is rejected by Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}mixture\text{-}inversion}\); the other recorded extra roots are either outside \((0,1)\) or have the displayed infeasible root values.  Direct rational substitution of the four legal records in (C10), followed by comparison with the common endpoint value at the arc endpoints, yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
 L_{\mathrm{sep}}
 &=\frac{94711}{277400}-\frac{2553}{5650}
 =-\frac{3461701}{31346200}
 \in[-110434471/10^9,-110434470/10^9],\\
 R_{\mathrm{sep}}
 &=\frac{212689}{302600}-\frac{1797}{12475}
 =\frac{84380923}{150997400}
 \in[558823681/10^9,558823682/10^9].
\end{aligned}                                                           \tag{19}
\]
Exact interval subtraction of (18)--(19) gives
\[
 L-L_{\mathrm{sep}}
 \in[2934168/10^9,2934170/10^9],
 \qquad
 R_{\mathrm{sep}}-R
 \in[19313713/10^9,19313715/10^9].                                     \tag{20}
\]
Both endpoint inclusions in (13) are therefore strict at the witness.

Finally, we prove relative-open stability without assuming persistence of an active branch.  Let \(\gamma\geq1\) vary near \(16\).  On the interior square, the coordinatewise logit map writes the exposure region as \(|s_1-s_0|\leq\log\gamma\).  If \(\gamma_n\to\gamma\), keep \((s_0+s_1)/2\) fixed and truncate \(s_1-s_0\) to \([-log\gamma_n,\log\gamma_n]\).  The inverse-logit pair belongs to \(D_{\gamma_n}\) and converges to the original pair.  The two constant corners belong to every \(D_\gamma\); conversely, every limit of pairs in \(D_{\gamma_n}\) satisfies the two closed cross-product inequalities for \(D_\gamma\).  Therefore
\[
 d_H(D_{\gamma_n},D_\gamma)\longrightarrow0.                           \tag{21}
\]

Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}mixture\text{-}inversion}\) and Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}closed\text{-}chart\text{-}extension}\) make all endpoint objectives jointly continuous in the interior observed summaries, finite positive budgets, and posterior pair.  Given minimizers in \(D_{\gamma_n}\), compactness supplies subsequential limits, (21) makes them feasible in \(D_\gamma\), and joint continuity gives the lower-limit inequality for the minima.  Approximating a minimizer in \(D_\gamma\) by points in \(D_{\gamma_n}\) gives the upper-limit inequality.  Maxima follow by negation, and the same argument applies to all four armwise separate extrema.  Thus \(L-L_{\mathrm{sep}}\) and \(R_{\mathrm{sep}}-R\) are continuous at the witness.  Their positive lower bounds in (20) remain positive on a sufficiently small relatively open neighborhood of the displayed interior law and finite budgets.  This proves stable strict tightening.

statements.statement: For arbitrary real interior observed summaries, \(\mathfrak T_0(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) admits on every compact finite-budget box \(\mathcal B\) a finite semialgebraic stratification, with defining formulas over the coefficient field \(K_{\mathrm{in}}\); its lower-dimensional strata contain all optimizer ties, legal-root collisions, constant-\(U\) contacts, and stationary continua.  The lower endpoint \(L\) is continuous and coordinatewise nonincreasing in \((\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\).  If the observed summaries and endpoints of \(\mathcal B\) are rational or real algebraic, \(\mathsf{ATLAS}\), separately from the fixed-input procedure \(\mathsf{CERT}\), terminates and returns exact quantifier-free sign cells on the complement of \(\mathfrak T_0\) and exact algebraic strata on the surface; rational isolating intervals are returned only after zero-dimensional specialization.
statements.justification: The tipping surface converts three interpretable confounding budgets into the exact frontier at which a positive causal conclusion fails.
statements.gap: Masten--Poirier study breakdown frontiers for other relaxations; the common-\(U\) frontier is multibudget, algebraic, and branch-switching.
statements.consumer: Sensitivity reports can display which combinations of treatment and outcome associations, rather than one arbitrary scalar, overturn the sign conclusion.
statements.proof_tex:
The proof uses first-order semialgebraic elimination to construct the atlas and compact-set arguments for monotonicity and continuity.  All observed summaries are real with \(0<p_x,r_{a,x}<1\), and every budget lies in the compact finite box \(\mathcal B\subset[1,\infty)^3\).

For each stratum, Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}one\text{-}arc\text{-}endpoint\text{-}reduction}\) represents every non-point-identified endpoint on
\[
 (w_0,w_1)=\left(\frac{\Gamma_A t}{1+(\Gamma_A-1)t},t\right),
 \qquad 0\leq t\leq1,                                                   \tag{22}
\]
and represents the forward arc by complementing \(U\).  Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}complete\text{-}semialgebraic\text{-}certificate}\) shows that every legal root, analytic outcome branch, stationary condition, endpoint condition, and objective comparison in (22) has a finite polynomial description after adjoining legal mixture-root variables.  Reciprocal endpoints are encoded by \(\Gamma_a\vartheta_a=1\), legal because \(\Gamma_a\geq1\).  The strata \(\Gamma_A=1\), \(\Gamma_a=1\), \(t=0,1\), root collisions, and vanishing denominators are recorded separately.

Let \(\mathsf{Feas}_x(v,s;\gamma)\) be the resulting finite disjunction asserting that \(v\) contains legal canonical-arc and mixture-root variables and that the corresponding lower objective equals \(s\), where \(\gamma=(\Gamma_A,\Gamma_0,\Gamma_1)\).  The lower endpoint graph is exactly
\[
\begin{split}
 \operatorname{Graph}(\ell_x)=\{(\gamma,s):{}&
 \exists v\,\mathsf{Feas}_x(v,s;\gamma)\ \wedge\\
 &\neg\exists(v',s')\,[\mathsf{Feas}_x(v',s';\gamma)\wedge s'<s]\}.
\end{split}                                                             \tag{23}
\]
Compactness of \([0,1]\) and continuity of the legal-root objectives ensure that (23) contains an attained minimum, so it neither loses an infimum nor introduces a false endpoint.

Apply the finite projection-and-lifting construction proved in the certificate theorem to (23), treating the observed summaries and \(\gamma\) as coefficients.  Projection eliminates all quantified coordinates and partitions \(\mathcal B\) into finitely many sign-invariant semialgebraic cells over \(K_{\mathrm{in}}\).  On each cell the legal optimizer strata and their algebraic objective values are fixed.  Adjoin variables \((s_x)_{x\in\mathcal X}\), the graph equations (23), and
\[
 L=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\lambda_xs_x,
 \qquad L=0.                                                            \tag{24}
\]
Projection and lifting applied to this finite polynomial family give a finite semialgebraic stratification of \(\mathfrak T_0(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\cap\mathcal B\).  Adding branch-boundary polynomials, discriminants, legal-root Jacobian minors, and pairwise objective differences to the projection family records optimizer ties, legal-root collisions, constant-\(U\) contacts, and stationary continua as designated lower-dimensional cells in the joint parameter--optimizer stratification.  Such sets are retained rather than discarded by a generic resultant.

We next prove coordinatewise monotonicity.  By Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}outcome\text{-}budget\text{-}extrema}\),
\[
 q^-_{a,x}(w;\Gamma_a)
 =\min_{\theta\in[\Gamma_a^{-1},\Gamma_a]}q_{a,x}(w;\theta),
 \qquad
 q^+_{a,x}(w;\Gamma_a)
 =\max_{\theta\in[\Gamma_a^{-1},\Gamma_a]}q_{a,x}(w;\theta).           \tag{25}
\]
If \(\Gamma_1\) increases, the first interval expands, so \(q^-_{1,x}\) cannot increase.  If \(\Gamma_0\) increases, the second interval expands, so \(q^+_{0,x}\) cannot decrease.  Therefore \(H_x^-=q^-_{1,x}-q^+_{0,x}\) cannot increase under either enlargement.  If \(\Gamma_A'\geq\Gamma_A\), each cross-product inequality defining \(D_{A,x}(\Gamma_A)\) remains true at \(\Gamma_A'\), whence
\[
 D_{A,x}(\Gamma_A)\subseteq D_{A,x}(\Gamma_A').                        \tag{26}
\]
Minimizing the pointwise nonincreasing objective over the enlarged set proves that every \(\ell_x\), and hence \(L=\sum_x\lambda_x\ell_x\) with \(\lambda_x>0\), is coordinatewise nonincreasing.

For continuity, Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}mixture\text{-}inversion}\) and Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}closed\text{-}chart\text{-}extension}\) make \(q_{a,x}\) jointly continuous in the posterior pair and every finite positive tilt.  Taking the minimum or maximum over the compact interval in (25) makes \(q^-_{a,x}\) and \(q^+_{a,x}\) jointly continuous in the posterior pair and finite outcome budget.

It remains to control the moving exposure region.  Put \(c=\log\Gamma_A\).  In the interior square, with \(s_a=\operatorname{logit}(w_a)\), the two exposure inequalities are equivalent to
\[
 |s_1-s_0|\leq c.                                                       \tag{27}
\]
If \(c_n\to c\), keep \((s_0+s_1)/2\) fixed and truncate \(s_1-s_0\) to \([ -c_n,c_n]\); the inverse-logit pair lies in \(D_{A,x}(e^{c_n})\) and converges to the original pair.  The constant corners belong to every region.  Conversely, every convergent sequence of feasible pairs has a feasible limit because the cross-product inequalities are closed.  Thus \(D_{A,x}(e^{c_n})\) converges in Hausdorff distance to \(D_{A,x}(e^c)\), including \(c=0\), where the limit is the diagonal.

On the compact product of the posterior square and a finite budget neighborhood, the lower objective is uniformly continuous.  Evaluating the two minima at nearest feasible points in the two Hausdorff-close regions bounds their difference by that uniform-continuity modulus.  Therefore each \(\ell_x\), and hence the finite weighted sum \(L\), is continuous.

If the summaries and box endpoints are rational or real algebraic, every projection coefficient is an effective element of \(K_{\mathrm{in}}\).  Euclidean remainder sequences, exact algebraic-number sign tests, and the finite projection-and-lifting recursion terminate and return exact quantifier-free sign cells and algebraic optimizer strata.  Signed-remainder isolation returns rational isolating intervals after a zero-dimensional specialization.  A positive-dimensional stratum is returned by exact sign conditions rather than by a purported isolating interval.  This is exactly the contract of \(\mathsf{ATLAS}\), distinct from the fixed-input contract of \(\mathsf{CERT}\).

statements.statement: If \(\Gamma_A=1\), then \(w_{0,x}=w_{1,x}=\pi_x\) for every \(x\), so \(L=R=\sum_x\lambda_x(r_{1,x}-r_{0,x})\).  If \(\Gamma_0=\Gamma_1=1\), then on the strictly positive chart the two joint-cell equalities force \(\mu_{a,0,x}=\mu_{a,1,x}=r_{a,x}\) for every \((a,x)\); continuity of the endpoint objectives gives the same point-identification formula on the closed class.
statements.justification: These reductions are mandatory checks that either absent treatment-confounder association or absent outcome-confounder association removes bias.
statements.gap: The reductions are implicit in fixed-parameter analyses but have not been stated as boundary faces of a sharp bounded envelope.
statements.consumer: They provide unit tests for implementations and an interpretable origin for the tipping atlas.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix (x\in\mathcal X).  We treat the two stated boundary regimes separately.

First suppose that (Gamma_A=1).  By Definition (mathrm{def{:}exposure  ext{-}region}), every ((w_0,w_1)\in D_{A,x}) obeys
\[
w_1(1-w_0)\leq w_0(1-w_1)
\quad\text{and}\quad
w_0(1-w_1)\leq w_1(1-w_0).
\]
The two cross-products are therefore equal.  Expanding and cancelling their common term gives
\[
w_1-w_0w_1=w_0-w_0w_1,
\qquad\text{hence}\qquad
w_1=w_0.
\]
This algebra remains valid at the boundary values (0) and (1).  Write the common value as (w_x).  The prevalence formula in Definition (mathrm{def{:}adjusted  ext{-}arm  ext{-}mean}) then yields
\[
\pi_x=p_xw_x+(1-p_x)w_x=w_x=w_{a,x},
\qquad a\in\{0,1\}.
\]
For every feasible outcome-odds value (  heta>0), Definition (mathrm{def{:}adjusted  ext{-}arm  ext{-}mean}) consequently gives
\[
q_{a,x}(w_x,w_x;\theta)-r_{a,x}
=(\pi_x-w_{a,x})(m_1-m_0)=0.
\]
Thus, by Definition (mathrm{def{:}common  ext{-}u  ext{-}endpoints}),
\[
q^-_{a,x}(w_x,w_x)=q^+_{a,x}(w_x,w_x)=r_{a,x}
\]
and
\[
H^-_x(w_x,w_x)=H^+_x(w_x,w_x)=r_{1,x}-r_{0,x}.
\]
Because every point of (D_{A,x}) is diagonal when (Gamma_A=1), both endpoint objectives are constant on the whole feasible region.  Hence
\[
\ell_x=\upsilon_x=r_{1,x}-r_{0,x}.
\]
Summing over the finite support (mathcal X), as prescribed by Definition (mathrm{def{:}common  ext{-}u  ext{-}endpoints}), proves
\[
L=R=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\lambda_x(r_{1,x}-r_{0,x}).
\]
The strictly positive pair (w_{0,x}=w_{1,x}=1/2) belongs to (D_{A,x}).  The exact equality for both the interior and closed maintained classes in Theorem (mathrm{thm{:}sharp  ext{-}common  ext{-}u  ext{-}envelope}) therefore shows that this singleton, rather than merely an outer bound, is the causal ATE identified set and that its endpoint is attained in the interior class.

Now suppose that (Gamma_0=Gamma_1=1).  Then (Gamma_a=1) for each (a\in\{0,1\}).  Take any
\(widetilde P\in\mathcal M^{\circ}(P_{\mathrm{obs}},\Gamma_A,1,1)\), and fix ((a,x)).  Define
\[
c_{u,x}=\widetilde P(U=u,X=x),
\qquad u\in\{0,1\}.
\]
Strict positivity in Definition (mathrm{def{:}positive  ext{-}common  ext{-}u  ext{-}class}) implies
\[
c_{u,x}>0
\quad\text{and}\quad
0<\mu_{a,u,x}<1.
\]
Definitions of (eta) and (mu) give the factorizations
\[
\eta_{a,1,u,x}=c_{u,x}\mu_{a,u,x},
\qquad
\eta_{a,0,u,x}=c_{u,x}(1-\mu_{a,u,x}).
\]
Assumptions (mathrm{ass{:}outcome  ext{-}odds  ext{-}upper}) and (mathrm{ass{:}outcome  ext{-}odds  ext{-}lower}), specialized to (Gamma_a=1), supply the two opposite inequalities and hence the equality
\[
\eta_{a,1,1,x}\eta_{a,0,0,x}
=\eta_{a,1,0,x}\eta_{a,0,1,x}.
\]
Substitution of the preceding factorizations gives
\[
c_{1,x}c_{0,x}\mu_{a,1,x}(1-\mu_{a,0,x})
=c_{0,x}c_{1,x}\mu_{a,0,x}(1-\mu_{a,1,x}).
\]
Division by the strictly positive quantity (c_{0,x}c_{1,x}), followed by expansion and cancellation, yields
\[
\mu_{a,1,x}-\mu_{a,1,x}\mu_{a,0,x}
=\mu_{a,0,x}-\mu_{a,0,x}\mu_{a,1,x},
\qquad\text{so}\qquad
\mu_{a,1,x}=\mu_{a,0,x}.
\]
